item.title: US stocks: Dow rockets 1,100 points, S&P over 2% as oil slide cools inflation worries; Nvidia slumps
item.description: US stocks experienced a notable upswing on Monday following a decline in oil prices that calmed inflation worries and propelled market growth. The S&P 500 rebounded significantly after the midterm elections, with gains in nine sector indexes. Nvidia's shares fell amid uncertainty over CEO Jensen Huang's future. Analysts argue the stock market's prior drop was exaggerated, with investors now keenly awaiting inflation reports to gauge Federal Reserve responses.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: US stocks rallied sharply on Monday as falling oil prices eased inflation concerns and helped the S&P 500 rebound from its steepest weekly decline since April 2025. Technology shares also surged, even as AI heavyweight Nvidia tumbled amid uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang, Reuters reported.The S&P 500 climbed 172.97 points, or 2.34%, to close at 7,549.83. The Nasdaq Composite gained 671.13 points, or 2.73%, to 25,250.55, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,104.20 points, or 2.16%, to 52,394.36.Stocks fell sharply last week after Democrats swept the US midterm elections, fuelling concerns that tighter regulations could threaten the durability of the artificial intelligence trade.Nine of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors gained more than 1% on Monday. Industrials and consumer discretionary led the advance, rising about 4% each.The broader market rallied despite a steep decline in Nvidia, the world’s second-most valuable company. Its shares touched their lowest intraday level since March 31 as investors questioned Huang’s future at the chipmaker following an internal investigation into whether he had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.“The AI story is not going away if people are worried about that. The Democrats are not going to destroy AI. They can’t. It’s got a life of its own. They can put regulation around it, but they’re certainly not stopping it,” Ken Polcari, partner and chief market strategist at SlateStone Wealth in Jupiter, Florida told Reuters.A sharp decline in crude-oil prices provided further support by easing concerns about inflation after US President Donald Trump played down the likelihood of renewed strikes on Iran.“Oil prices for sure, if they’re down, that’s certainly adding fuel to the fire,” Polcari said.Investors are now awaiting key inflation reports. The Labor Department is scheduled to release October’s Consumer Price Index on Tuesday, followed by the Producer Price Index on Friday.Some Wall Street analysts described last week’s sell-off as an overreaction. Morgan Stanley and UBS said the rout in AI-linked stocks appeared excessive, arguing that the risk of severe restrictions on data-centre development remained low despite Democratic majorities in Congress.Expectations for an interest-rate increase at the Federal Reserve’s December meeting remained above 80%, according to CME FedWatch. October’s strong jobs report was seen as giving the central bank room to continue raising rates, even as oil prices eased.Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said on Monday that the central bank should adjust monetary policy “with care” as it formulates its response to inflation.Chipmakers rallied strongly. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped about 7% after tumbling more than 12% last week, its steepest weekly decline since the week ended April 4, 2025.Nvidia was the index’s only decliner on Monday, while Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices provided the biggest boosts.KKR shares advanced after the investment firm reported record quarterly profit. Constellation Energy, which has exposure to the AI infrastructure buildout, surged more than 10% after its adjusted third-quarter profit exceeded expectations.Berkshire Hathaway’s Class A shares also gained after the conglomerate reported lower third-quarter profit.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: Citi downgrades US stocks to 'neutral' as AI sell-off, regulatory risks mount
item.description: Citigroup strategists have downgraded US equities to neutral due to ongoing market volatility and regulatory concerns. This decision follows a significant sell-off that erased $3 trillion from the market value of S&P 500 companies. The strategists expressed worries about the potential for key indices like Nasdaq to shift into net-short territory. They also adjusted global and European technology sector ratings to neutral while upgrading healthcare stocks.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Citigroup strategists downgraded US stocks to “neutral” from “overweight,” saying they wanted to see cleaner investor positioning and more stable sentiment towards artificial intelligence stocks following a sharp sell-off driven by concerns about surging AI spending and tighter regulation, Reuters reported.“We worry that positioning on key indices, such as the Nasdaq, could reset lower into net-short territory,” strategists led by Beata Manthey said in a note on Monday.For live updates on US Markets, click hereCiti also cut its ratings on the global and European technology sectors to “neutral” from “overweight.”Democrat victories in last week’s US midterm elections, including in states where opposition to new data centres has grown, raised fears that stricter regulations could slow the AI infrastructure buildout that helped propel stocks to record highs this year.The sell-off erased about $3 trillion from the market value of S&P 500 companies.“Volatility has now turned more broad-based, with a sizable sell-off across regions and sectors in recent days,” Citi told Reuters.Also Read: Fed’s Barkin urges rate policy caution, Goolsbee warns of inflation concerns as AI risks loomThe brokerage upgraded European equities excluding the UK, citing their lower exposure to technology-sector volatility and greater sensitivity to falling oil prices.At the sector level, Citi raised global healthcare and European food and beverage stocks to “overweight” from “neutral.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: US stocks: Dow Jones rallies 500 points, Nasdaq over 2% as chip stocks rebound; Nvidia probe weighs
item.description: Wall Street's indexes climbed as investors honed in on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's investigation and awaited crucial inflation data. Nvidia's shares faced declines due to worries over foreign intelligence, yet analysts proposed that the sell-off in AI stocks was potentially overblown. Tech giants like Microsoft and Alphabet, along with chip manufacturers such as Marvell and Broadcom, enjoyed substantial gains.
item.dc:creator: Somanjali Das
item.content:encoded: Wall Street’s main indexes rose on Monday as investors looked past last week’s AI-related concerns and awaited further clarity on the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Reuters reported.Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 569.51 points, or 1.11%, to 51,855.24. The S&P 500 rose 109.17 points, or 1.48%, to 7,462.90, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 616 points, or 2.53%, to 24,931.00.The rebound comes as a crucial week begins, which could help determine whether last week’s sell-off after the midterms was overdone or justified. Analysts cautioned that several risks continued to weigh on market sentiment.Nvidia shares fell 5.6% after an internal investigation into whether a foreign intelligence operation had targeted Huang raised questions about his future at the AI chipmaker. Nvidia is the world’s second-most valuable company.“This was just the cherry on top for investors looking to pull out of AI-linked stocks. It’s a very bad headline that’s affecting tech stocks,” Nadia El Bilassy, senior market analyst at Equiti Group, told Reuters.El Bilassy said the focus on Nvidia could ease later in the week “when we have more important things to discuss, like the inflation data.”The US Labor Department is scheduled to release October’s Consumer Price Index report on Tuesday. Economists polled by Reuters expect inflation to have risen 2.7% from a year earlier.Concerns about a potential interest-rate hike in December also persisted following stronger-than-expected US jobs data for October.Nine of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors traded higher, led by consumer discretionary and communication services.Morgan Stanley and UBS said last week’s rout in AI-linked stocks appeared overdone. The Wall Street brokerages argued that the prospect of severe restrictions on data-centre development under a Democrat-controlled Congress was unlikely to materialise.Chip stocks rise as investors assess earningsChip stocks advanced, with Marvell Technology gaining 5% and Broadcom rising 6.5%. Intel and Qualcomm climbed nearly 2% each.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 3.3% after recording its steepest weekly loss since March 2025 last week.Among major technology companies, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon gained between 2.5% and 5%. Elon Musk-led Tesla and SpaceX rose 4.5% each.KKR shares gained 1% after the investment firm reported record quarterly profit. Constellation Energy, which has exposure to the AI boom, rose 2.8% after its adjusted third-quarter profit exceeded expectations.Of the 335 S&P 500 companies that had reported earnings as of Thursday, 82.4% beat estimates, according to Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.Berkshire Hathaway’s Class B shares slipped 0.1% after the conglomerate reported lower third-quarter profit.Advancing stocks outnumbered decliners by 3.87 to 1 on the New York Stock Exchange and by 2.32 to 1 on the Nasdaq.The S&P 500 recorded four new 52-week highs and two new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite registered 36 new highs and 80 new lows.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

item.title: US market remains tied to tech stocks despite sharp AI sell-off
item.description: The US stock market is currently experiencing a significant pullback in technology and AI-related stocks. Investors are concerned that Democratic victories in the midterm elections may result in reduced data center spending. Despite recent declines, the technology sector remains dominant within the S&P 500 index. Upcoming technology earnings reports and the potential IPO of AI lab Anthropic are closely watched by investors.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Despite the sharp pullback in artificial intelligence stocks, the US equity market remains heavily dependent on the technology sector, leaving investors alert to risks that could disrupt the trade in the coming weeks, Reuters reported.A month-long decline in technology and AI-linked stocks culminated this week in the S&P 500 technology sector’s steepest one-day fall in more than six years. Investors fear that Democratic victories in the midterm elections could slow the data-centre spending that has helped drive the broader market rally, Reuters reported.Technology nevertheless remains the largest sector in the S&P 500 by a wide margin. Although its influence has eased slightly, the sector still accounted for more than 35% of the index’s market capitalisation as of Thursday’s close.“Because so much of technology is AI-sensitive, it’s going to have an impact on the entire sector, and that sector carries so much weight within the S&P 500,” said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth Management. “So weakness in AI is going to drag down tech, which drags down the S&P 500.”Technology’s share of the S&P 500 remains above the level reached at the height of the dot-com bubble in 2000.The sector’s weighting also understates AI’s overall influence on the market. Alphabet, Amazon and Meta Platforms—three of the largest spenders on data centres—are classified outside the technology sector.Technology’s dominance reflects the enormous gains it has recorded during the US bull market that began in October 2022. Even after the latest decline, the sector is up more than 200% over that period—nearly twice the S&P 500’s gain.Several major beneficiaries of the AI boom also retain substantial year-to-date gains despite the recent sell-off. Sandisk shares remained up about 250% in 2026, while Dell Technologies had gained roughly 160% and Micron Technology was up 140%.Following a partial rebound on Friday, the S&P 500 was up nearly 8% for the year, while the technology sector had gained about 11%.“If somebody is in a profit-taking mode, there are still profits to be had,” said Chuck Carlson, CEO of Horizon Investment Services, according to Reuters.The sell-off has also made technology stocks appear less expensive, at least by one widely used measure. The sector’s forward price-to-earnings ratio, based on projected earnings over the next 12 months, fell to 17.1 as of Thursday, according to LSEG Datastream. It had exceeded 32 in October 2025.By comparison, the broader S&P 500 traded at a forward P/E ratio of 17.9. This marked the first time since 2017 that the technology sector’s valuation had fallen below that of the overall index.The valuation decline suggests that “arguably … the market is already pricing in a lot of bad news,” said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services. “We are moving toward a situation where a little good news could go a long way,” Lerner wrote in a note on Thursday.Investors are now watching several potential catalysts that could determine the direction of the AI trade.Anthropic IPODevelopments surrounding AI laboratory Anthropic’s planned initial public offering could influence sentiment towards the sector.Reuters reported on Thursday that prospective investors were questioning whether the company could begin its IPO roadshow next week in time for a November listing. The discussions partly reflect the impact of the sharp decline in technology stocks.Technology earningsAlthough most companies have already reported third-quarter results, several closely watched earnings releases remain.Cloud-computing company CoreWeave, which has been at the centre of concerns about financing the AI infrastructure buildout, is scheduled to report on Tuesday. AI bellwether Nvidia is due to report on November 17, followed by Dell on November 24.Macroeconomic backdropDevelopments in the US-Israeli conflict with Iran are also expected to influence the broader market. Expectations that the change in Congress could help end the conflict pushed oil prices lower this week, providing support to equities.Investors, however, remain wary of a renewed escalation following the midterm elections. They are also closely monitoring the outlook for interest rates and the extent to which the Federal Reserve may raise borrowing costs to contain inflation.Next week’s Consumer Price Index report will provide an important test of that outlook.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
